messages:
amy: Quick sync — FintechCo wants Private deployment POC. They need guidance on connectivity (PrivateLink vs VPC peering), exact firewall/SG allowlist, egress IPs for compliance, and any pricing delta for private endpoints. POC target: next Wed.

devin: Quick clarifying q: is customer doing our Private control plane (interface endpoints) or full on-prem package? That changes IP/port list.

amy: They want Redwood Private in their AWS account (we'll hand off control-plane endpoints into their VPC). So PrivateLink/interface endpoints is preferred by their infra folks.

rita: From netops: if we use interface endpoints they only need SG rules outbound to the endpoint ENIs, simpler. For peering they'd have to allow our pod/subnet ranges — larger blast radius. Also what about static egress IPs? They need allowlist entries for downstream partners.

devin: Short version — recommend interface endpoint (PrivateLink) for the POC. Notes: 1) TLS only (443) to control plane; 2) metrics/health maybe to 8443 if they opt in; 3) no inbound ports open to Redwood from internet.

rita: Can you paste the SG snippet we usually hand to customers?

devin: Yep — copy/paste below (AWS SG example):
```
# Allow outbound to Redwood control plane endpoints (TLS)
Type: Outbound
Protocol: TCP
PortRange: 443
Destination: aws interface endpoint ENI security group (customer-managed)

# If you want metrics/ops (optional)
Protocol: TCP
PortRange: 8443
Destination: 10.12.200.0/24  # example ops subnet
```
Also include egress NAT to preserve source IP if they need a fixed egress from their VPC — we can provide a list of our ingestion IPs for allowlisting but with PrivateLink it's usually not needed.

carla: Security: they asked for an official list of IPs/CIDRs for allowlisting and whether we support mTLS between their proxy and our endpoints. Also need confirmation on whether any customer data touches a public network during handshake.

devin: mTLS: yes for control plane APIs we support client certs (optional), and TLS with strict cert validation is default. Regarding IPs: for PrivateLink, traffic stays in AWS backbone; there is no public egress. For any optional outbound (e.g., to our support/metrics if they opt in) we can provide a small set of IP ranges — we'll supply that in the SOW.

rita: Enterprise blocker: their infra team refuses cross-account peering unless CIDRs are non-overlapping and there is an approved routing policy. PrivateLink avoids cross-account routing so good. Also need to confirm acceptance flow for interface endpoints (they need to create and accept, or we provide a partner service?).

devin: Acceptance flow: customer creates interface endpoint in their VPC to our service name (we document the service name per region). There's an accept step in some setups but for AWS PrivateLink to our managed service it's typically auto-available once they use the service name. We'll send exact service-name string and IAM policy snippet.

amy: Pricing/POC asks from procurement: is there an extra per-endpoint or data egress cost we should anticipate? They also asked about Dedicated capacity vs Private one-time setup fees.

devin: Per-endpoint: normal AWS interface endpoint charges apply on their side. For Redwood: Private deployment has a setup fee (one-time) + monthly private license if they want an isolated control plane. Dedicated capacity and reserved GPU pools are separate add-ons. I'll ask finance for exact numbers and paste here.

amy: Perfect. Timeline: Rita, can you confirm the minimal SG rules and a short preflight checklist we can share with customer by EOD today? If we can get that + SOW numbers, procurement can sign and we start next Wed.

rita: On it — will drop a concise preflight checklist with exact service-name, SG example, and the optional NAT/EIP notes in ~2h.

network-bot: deploy-checklist job queued: private-endpoint-docs/latest -> staging (job #4398) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

amy: thanks — once we have the checklist I'll attach to the POC kickoff email and loop in their security reviewer (carla).

carla: When you send the checklist, include an explicit statement about data-in-transit staying on AWS internal network for PrivateLink and the available encryption/mTLS options. I'll review for SOC2 questions.

devin: Will do. Also adding this note for infra: if customer still prefers peering for some reason, we require an architecture diagram (CIDRs, route tables) and we'll need to coordinate a maintenance window for route propagation testing. PrivateLink avoids that extra coordination, which is why it's our default for enterprise POCs.

amy: Great thread. I'll compile notes and follow up with the customer. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
